sections.title: Basic Concept of Pie Chart
sections.content: A Pie Chart is a circular graph that represents the whole data as 100 percent. The complete circle equals 360 degrees. Each sector shows the percentage share of a category. For example, if total income is ₹1,00,000 and 20 percent is spent on rent, then rent share is 20 percent or 72 degrees.

sections.title: Relation Between Percentage and Degrees
sections.content: 100 percent equals 360 degrees. 1 percent equals 3.6 degrees. To convert percentage to degrees multiply by 3.6. To convert degrees to percentage divide by 3.6. Example: 90 degrees equals 25 percent.

sections.title: Finding Actual Value from Percentage
sections.content: Actual value equals percentage multiplied by total divided by 100. Example: If total sales are ₹5,00,000 and electronics share is 30 percent, then electronics sales equal ₹1,50,000.

sections.title: Finding Percentage from Value
sections.content: Percentage equals part divided by total multiplied by 100. Example: If food expense is ₹40,000 out of ₹2,00,000, then percentage is 20 percent.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content: 1. Percentage to degree equals percentage multiplied by 3.6. 2. Degree to percentage equals degree divided by 3.6. 3. Actual value equals percentage multiplied by total divided by 100.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting that total circle is 360 degrees. 2. Comparing percentages without checking total value. 3. Calculation errors while multiplying by 3.6.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In a Pie Chart, the whole circle represents 100 percent or 360 degrees. Always check the total value first. Convert percentage to actual value before comparing categories.

tricks.title: Start with 10 percent method
tricks.example: 10 percent of ₹80,000 is ₹8,000. So 30 percent is ₹24,000.

tricks.title: Use 1 percent method
tricks.example: 1 percent of ₹2,00,000 is ₹2,000. So 18 percent is ₹36,000.

tricks.title: 20 percent trick
tricks.example: 10 percent of ₹70,000 is ₹7,000, so 20 percent is ₹14,000.

tricks.title: 5 percent trick
tricks.example: 10 percent of ₹60,000 is ₹6,000, so 5 percent is ₹3,000.

tricks.title: Check total 100 percent
tricks.explanation: Add all percentages to confirm total is 100 percent.
tricks.example: If total is 98 percent, then 2 percent data is missing.

tricks.title: Difference shortcut
tricks.explanation: Find difference in percentage first, then calculate value.
tricks.example: Difference between 40 percent and 25 percent is 15 percent. 15 percent of ₹2,00,000 is ₹30,000.
